finding.what: Caption 10 says 'Women did worse in 2 of 6' at 54.2 s while the picture still shows the F pair (6 / 7); the extruded 2 and the neon only land at 55.5 s, so the result is told before it is seen.
finding.why: The reveal frame should land with its caption (54.2 s), not 1.4 s after it; with dv0 45.5 and dvStep 1.4 the F pair still lands at 53.1 s and holds.

finding.what: After the turn has landed (split1 45.4 s) the headline still reads the stale overall '30' (WOMEN ADMITTED %) over the six department pairs until 46.5 s; a stale ratio sits over the new evidence.
finding.why: Call department A the moment the slabs have landed, so the headline never contradicts the picture under it.

applied.old: 51 % of men applied to A or B. 7 % of women.
applied.new: 1,385 of 2,691 men applied to A or B; 133 of 1,835 women.

finding.what: Caption 11 gives '51 % ... 7 %' at 58.6 s, before the bracket's counts appear (mixT 58.8) and 2 s before the picture turns them to percentages (mixPct 60.6): ratio before count inside the mix beat.
finding.proposed_value: 1,385 of 2,691 men applied to A or B; 133 of 1,835 women.
finding.why: Counts before ratios: the caption now matches the counts on screen at 58.8 s; the picture supplies 51 % and 7 % at 60.6 s. All four numbers are claims (menAB, womenAB, menApplied, womenApplied).

applied.old: Women did worse in 2 of 6, by 3 and 4 points.
applied.new: Women did worse in 2 of 6, and ahead in 4.

finding.what: The reveal caption frames only the negative ('worse in 2 of 6, by 3 and 4 points'); the reversal the picture shows is women ahead in four of six.
finding.proposed_value: Women did worse in 2 of 6, and ahead in 4.
finding.why: Puts the paradox in words a manager repeats: worse overall, ahead in most parts. 4 is the womenBetter claim and was already in this caption.

finding.what: The per-department rate ledger above the pairs (62% 82%, 63% 68% ... 6% 7%) is the evidence of the reversal, yet it is set at the 20-unit floor of its range; at 480 x 270 it reads as chrome.
finding.why: Results never in the smallest face: the ledger is what lets the viewer count four women-higher pairs from the picture.

finding.what: Pairs E and F sit close; their ledger labels (28% 24%, 6% 7%) and pins crowd each other, and will touch once pinRate grows.
finding.why: More air between department groups gives each pair its own column of labels and makes 'six separate comparisons' read at a glance.

finding.what: The side view occupies about a third of the frame height (y 120-210 of 270); the lit heights that carry the reversal are small.
finding.why: About 7 % larger slabs in the side view, still clear of the headline and caption; the lit-height comparison is the picture that has to win.

finding.what: Each department pair holds about 0.4 s between 0.9 s morphs (63 68 at 48.5-49.0, 37 34 at 49.5-50.0); the numbers are half-formed in a third of the frames.
finding.why: Shorter morphs leave a readable hold per pair (borrowed from draft b's longer pair holds).

finding.what: Department call-outs step every 1.3 s; with the earlier dv0 there is room for a slightly longer step before the reveal.
finding.why: A at 45.5, F at 52.5 (lands 53.1), reveal 54.4: each pair gets about 0.8 s clean hold after the morph.

finding.what: The empty turntable ring spans the whole frame in the HOOK and MONDAY and its tick marks cross the caption line and the hook headline.
finding.why: The smallest documented ring keeps the instrument but pulls its ticks off the caption and headline text.

finding.what: In the front view the camera at 27 degrees shows the column tops, and the arriving boxes on the tops run through the MEN / WOMEN APPLIED labels.
finding.why: A lower, more frontal view reads 'men taller' as pure height and shows less of the busy tops under the labels; it also flattens the ring off the caption.
